Celestine D.
Director intelligent automation at AMISEQ
I think the best feature is the ease of Control Room, which is better in UiPath Platform compared to Automation Anywhere. My team has used the vendor's UiPath Academy courses. The biggest benefit is that the courses provide the latest and greatest features coming up in the product, and the team gets trained with those materials. We have not hit a roadblock with the UiPath user community, but a community is always useful wherever it exists. I am able to automate actions or responses according to the type of content in the messages with UiPath Communications Mining. The help from Communications Mining comes down to the logging capabilities of the platform. Every single transaction and every action taken by the automation is logged. Based on that, we can clearly bring out positive feedback to the client, as well as exceptions being triggered and processed. We can manage all of this as part of the platform logging. UiPath Platform also has a built-in AI agent that helps us build the flows, and we can choose the models from it. Code completions are part of the platform, so we do not have to use anything external.

Hemanth Pagadala
Senior Business Process Automation Engineer at a manufacturing company with 10,001+ employees
The standard feature of UiPath Platform is UiPath Studio, which also includes a terminal and multiple cloud code extensions. This enhances the workflow, rendering a lot of work that used to take days into minutes or hours. Previously, I used to code manually integrated templates, naming each activity and running all the code with multiple unit tests and debugging each flow. This took a significant amount of time. Now, since there are code extensions available, I can give a detailed prompt and get a workflow done quickly. The testing also occurs at a much faster pace, and if there are multiple validation errors, the RMID packages are already generated. The modern activities have higher user engagement compared to classic activities, which had fewer features. The integration services are also effective, but utilizing the integrations and achieving scalability is straightforward since it operates on XAML, allowing me to create multiple XAMLs to enhance scalability. We mainly use UiPath Platform because it is low code compared to traditional approaches when AI was not involved. UiPath Platform makes it easy to learn, create RPA workflows, push to production, and obtain code reviews since it is virtually a low-code platform. This year, we have improved our project delivery speed significantly, moving into a product with much less time than traditional programming languages.

Sathyajith S
Technical Specialist - Platform Engineer at a financial services firm with 10,001+ employees
Some of the best features I can highlight in the UiPath Platform include its low-code development capabilities, which make it easy for developers to build and deploy automations. The drag-and-drop workflow design significantly reduces development effort and accelerates delivery, making it one of the platform's most valuable features. Another key capability is AI-powered Document Understanding, which extracts data from invoices, forms, emails, and other documents, significantly reducing manual data entry. Document Understanding is one of the most valuable features for automating document-intensive business processes and is widely used across my organization. UiPath Apps enable business users to quickly build business-facing applications on top of automation workflows, providing a user-friendly interface for interacting with automations. The feedback we have received indicates that these applications effectively bridge the gap between business users and backend automations, making automation solutions more accessible and user-friendly. UiPath Orchestrator provides centralized management of robots, queues, assets, schedules, and monitoring, ensuring strong governance and operational control. It offers excellent visibility into automation performance and provides a single platform for managing automation operations across the organization. The platform's integration capabilities work well with enterprise systems such as SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Microsoft 365, web applications, and legacy systems. This broad integration ecosystem helps reduce implementation complexity and enables seamless connectivity across business applications. AI Center allows organizations to deploy, manage, and integrate AI models into automation workflows, extending automation capabilities beyond rule-based processes. Additionally, Process Mining and Task Mining help identify automation opportunities by analysing real process data and user activities. These capabilities assist organizations in prioritizing automation initiatives based on measurable business value and operational insights. Considering all these features, including low-code development, Document Understanding, UiPath Apps, Orchestrator, integrations, AI Center, and Process Mining, I believe Document Understanding has had the greatest impact on my team. It is used across multiple business regions to automate the extraction of information from invoices, claims, forms, emails, and PDF documents. This capability eliminates a significant amount of manual data entry effort and delivers immediate value to operations teams, especially when combined with AI models and human validation workflows. Its ability to handle both structured and semi-structured documents makes it one of the most widely adopted and impactful features used by business users across my organization.

"Orchestrator is really good. It is the whole control center. We schedule, run, and monitor every bot from one place, a single unified platform, and it makes everything easier."
"UiPath Platform has positively impacted my organization because it has helped us automate processes and do things faster."
"For UiPath Platform's AI capabilities, I give the accuracy and reliability of output 10 out of 10."
Room for Improvement
Users cite expensive, confusing licensing, especially for smaller organizations. They seek simpler interfaces, clearer documentation, practical training, faster support. Developers want stronger debugging, more informative error logs, reliable version control, smoother upgrades. Organizations need less fragile selectors, broader native integrations, better performance at scale. They also want more accurate document extraction, mature AI capabilities, stronger governance, clearer operational dashboards.
"There are always areas for improvement in UiPath Platform, but I would say licensing is the biggest one."
"My feedback on improving those two points is the same: the bot-based licensing model has to shift."
"My rating of seven is based on scenarios when the product was down and there was no transparency whatsoever as to what was going on."
ROI
Organizations reported positive ROI from UiPath Platform through reduced manual effort, faster processing, fewer errors, avoided hiring. Reported invoice-processing times fell 60% to 80%; data accuracy exceeded 90%. Some organizations cited returns of 30% to 50%, thousands of hours saved annually, payback within six to twelve months. Others remained near breakeven because licensing, development, maintenance costs delayed financial gains.
Pricing
Enterprise buyers often find UiPath Platform expensive, particularly as unattended bots, Orchestrator, developer seats, and AI capabilities add to annual licensing costs. Licensing changes and feature-specific charges can make budgets difficult to forecast, though some organizations negotiate discounts. Setup is generally straightforward, while on-premises deployments may require additional infrastructure and implementation spending. A free Community edition supports evaluation, and organizations with well-utilized bots and multiple use cases report stronger returns.
"It is based on the use case. If the use case needs several bots, it gets expensive."
"The price of UiPath Platform in the Middle East region is a little bit high; having a lower price for the Middle East region would make it more attractive."
"I would definitely recommend UiPath, although the major concern is that it's not super cheap. Despite its higher price, I understand the complexity behind it since it's the most comprehensive RPA solution."
Popular Use Cases
Organizations primarily use UiPath Platform to automate repetitive, rule-based business processes and reduce manual effort and errors. Common applications include invoice processing, financial reconciliation, data entry, reporting, and extracting information from PDFs, emails, and spreadsheets. Bots also move data between systems such as SAP, Oracle, and Salesforce, supporting workflows across finance, HR, procurement, healthcare, and customer service.
Service and Support
Customers generally describe UiPath Platform support as helpful, knowledgeable, and responsive. Teams often receive answers within hours or a day, with calls and technical account managers helping resolve difficult issues. Forums, documentation, and UiPath Academy provide useful self-service help. Experiences vary by support tier: premium customers often get faster, more personalized assistance, while others report slow responses, repetitive questions, inconsistent frontline expertise, and delays with complex or urgent cases.
Deployment
Most users found UiPath Platform’s initial setup straightforward, particularly in the cloud, where accounts and robots could often be configured within minutes or hours. On-premises deployments took longer when teams needed to configure Orchestrator, servers, databases, permissions, and security. Timelines ranged from hours to months depending on organizational approvals and project scope. Beginners faced a learning curve, while documentation, community resources, and UiPath support helped teams resolve issues.
Scalability
Users generally find UiPath Platform highly scalable. Reusable workflows, parallel robots, Orchestrator, and cloud deployment help them expand automation across teams and workloads. They say growth depends on licensing, infrastructure, and how automations are designed. Some face high costs, slow provisioning, maintenance demands, or security restrictions. Others have not yet tested it at a large scale.
Stability
Users generally consider UiPath Platform stable and reliable, with little downtime and dependable production automations. Many rate its stability around eight or nine out of ten. Some encounter intermittent crashes, selector failures, or slowdowns, particularly after upgrades or under heavy workloads. Reliability also depends on sound bot design, sufficient infrastructure, and changes to applications being automated.
These insights are based on the in-depth reviews provided by peers to help you make a better buying decision.

UiPath Platform delivers a robust set of features that enhance automation and productivity. With components like Orchestrator, task management is optimized, facilitating better scalability. Users benefit from advanced AI and document understanding tools, boosting data handling accuracy and reducing errors. Despite its strengths, UiPath faces challenges with upgrading processes, AI enhancements, and user documentation. Integration and selector sensitivity issues, along with support and licensing complexities, highlight areas for potential improvement. Users request smoother deployment, error handling, and migration processes. Enhanced support for RHEL/Ubuntu, LINQ, and Lambda and improved real-time insights, automation recording, and scheduling are desired. Streamlining the experience for non-technical users with simplified workflows remains a priority.
What are the key features of UiPath Platform?
Drag-and-Drop Functionality: Allows users to design workflows easily without extensive technical skills.
Orchestrator: Enhances task management and enables scalable automation.
AI and Document Understanding: Improves data accuracy and minimizes errors.
System Integration: Offers seamless integration with SAP, CRM, Oracle, and more.
Active Community and Training: UiPath Academy provides resources for skill development.
What benefits should users look for in reviews?
Increased Efficiency: Reduction in manual workloads through automation of repetitive tasks.
Improved Accuracy: Enhanced data handling capabilities reduce errors.
Productivity Boost: Supports both attended and unattended automations to streamline operations.
Scalability: Ability to handle growing automation demands efficiently.
Integration Benefits: Easy integration with enterprise systems for streamlined operations.
UiPath Platform is widely implemented across sectors such as finance, healthcare, insurance, HR, IT, and supply chain to automate repetitive business tasks. Common uses include automating data entry, invoice processing, document management, report generation, and customer service operations. Organizations value the platform's ability to integrate seamlessly with systems like SAP, CRM, and Oracle, allowing for enhanced efficiency and accuracy in processing both structured and unstructured data.
UiPath Platform was previously known as UiPath Maestro, UiPath Apps, UiPath Agent Builder.

We have several use cases, but our main one is reducing manual work. The processes that require a lot of manual input and have a lot of human error are the focus. That could be, for instance, processes that have to do with invoicing, billing, reporting, and coding, which require a lot of man-hours, are very reliant on a human being available, and are time-sensitive. How has it helped my organization?
UiPath helps to implement end-to-end automation, although the discovery of processes, gathering requirements, and creating the design, all happen outside of UiPath. But the development, which is developing the bots, then testing and then deploying them, does happen end-to-end within UiPath.
The end-to-end development capability is important, but this is because every tool offers this and it is expected. That said, there is definitely room for improvement in that end-to-end should include process discovery. It is end-to-end, but those ends can extend further than what it currently is. In that sense, it's no different than other RPA tools.
Another way that UiPath improves the way our organization functions is that the robots can run 24/7. If you think about a human workforce, they work eight hours a day, they take days off, they get sick, they leave, and they take knowledge with them once they leave the company. But, the robots can be run non-stop 24/7, and each process can be scaled up. The same process can be run by one bot, or it can be run by 10 or 100 bots. This means that there's a lot more flexibility that the bots bring, especially for high-volume processes that perhaps even have some peaks, such as an end-of-month rush to produce invoices or meet a deadline or an end-of-financial-year crunch.
These robots have an easier time addressing and variability when it comes to volume. They really create a lot more scalability to where businesses can grow and know that they can meet the demands of the future. So, they're a lot more future-proof, whereas people are harder to rely on.

A company obviously needs to spend money on UiPath licenses and development costs, but those costs are oftentimes lower than the cost of that FTE, the full-time employee, whose work is getting automated. If you purely just think about the financial benefits, it's the lower staffing costs.
There is also the ability to free up people. This means that even if people aren't replaced and their salary isn't saved, what they can do is pivot their focus to, for instance, be a lot more customer-facing or do a lot more strategic or creative tasks that perhaps get pushed to the side because there's not a lot of time allocated towards performing them. Now, FTEs have a lot more capacity to contribute and perform tasks that still to this day cannot be automated, like creative thinking, complex decision-making on the spot, strategy, and just human interaction.

What I mean by that is that some jobs are replaced, and that's just simply because of that FTE saving that is usually the driver to justify the cost of development. It is literally just an if-else statement. It's a lot easier to quantify and therefore it's a lot easier to evaluate, and therefore the result is a lot more reliable. Recently, both platforms are converging onto each other and I feel like they're becoming more and more similar, but they still have a few things that are different.
One thing that stands out for me is that Blue Prism has wonderful debugging. It's a lot better than UiPath, and it's an all-in-one tool where the monitoring and the building of the robots happen in one application. The deployment is also really easy.
Blue Prism also offers online learning, which is great. They didn't use to have that offering, and I think that they got a lot of inspiration from UiPath. Their online courses have been great because previously when I was learning RPA, I had to use YouTube. Now, they have a whole Blue Prism university, which is amazing.
Blue Prism has inbuilt version control and a lot of other great features. They have a heavy emphasis on security and encryption, which UiPath perhaps needs to improve on. Companies such as banks, insurance agencies, and finance agencies are a lot more interested in Blue Prism because of its very strong security protocols. The encryption offering is a key requirement for companies that work with a lot of sensitive personal data.
How was the initial setup?
Setting up a new UiPath environment is very straightforward. The overall process is quite intuitive and easy-to-follow. I was really surprised how easy it is to create a new Orchestrator, setup new Tenants and Folders, assign licenses and invite users. If I'm ever unsure of how to configure something, there are plenty of practical guides and documentation out there to guide you through any hurdle.
What about the implementation team?
No
What was our ROI?
The areas of the organization with the most ROI from UiPath are operations, finance, HR, and sales. Those are the key departments, although it's across every organization because those departments have a lot of manual work-intensive processes that are the first contenders for automation.
What's my experience with pricing, setup cost, and licensing?
We have a yearly licensing model that gives us access to the development, test and production licenses. The cost of licensing is expensive and unfortunately, it's only going to increase. We manage the costs by taking lean approach towards dev and test licenses - making sure we are allocating and leveraging them efficiently. For production, we try to ensure that bot utilization is as close to 100% as possible, aiming to run the production bots near 24/7 in order to maximize value with the existing prod bot fleet.
What other advice do I have?
Part of automation is the analysis and optimization of processes because the analysis phase is a by-product of wanting to automate a task. If you want to automate something, you have to break it down into parts and really look at it and think, "How can I reduce this into a series of business rules, a series of decisions, or series of steps?" It's an exercise of process optimization in and of itself because a good practice in automation is to not just take what it is and automate it, but to think, "Does what is currently in place actually work? How can it be improved? How can it be streamlined? How can it be done in fewer steps?" It's a good chance to practice some process review, improvement, and transformation.
The idea is to make it optimal because the current process usually has unquestioned practices that maybe haven't been reviewed for a very long time. A lot of businesses say, "We've always done it this way," and they've never thought to revisit the approach. RPA gives you an opportunity to think about whether what you've always been doing will work when it's being done by a robot. Most often, the processes get streamlined through the requirements gathering phase, understanding the as-is, and then a key part of that is doing the process design, which is the to-be vision.
During that time, processes go through a few design iterations where they are optimized and streamlined because we want the robots to be as efficient as possible. This means performing as few steps as possible without sacrificing value and efficiency. It is important because any inefficiencies in a robot are going to scale with the number of times you're going to run that process. If you run a process a thousand times, and let's say there exists inefficiency that results in an extra minute being used, that could be shed if you were to review and optimize that process.
Ultimately, optimization is an important exercise because the benefits include a further capacity to run more automated processes, and less time is taken up by inefficient steps.
Something to be aware of is that updates to the platform have to be managed because any update could impact the performance of a bot that was built with an earlier version. To avoid having a newer version impact the performance of something that was built previously, all of the updates need to go through a due diligence process.
The biggest lesson that I have learned from UiPath is surprising; not everything needs to be automated. It feels weird to say it because thinking, "Well, I have this platform, I have these bots, why not just automate absolutely everything?", but the truth is that there are things that can be streamlined outside of RPAs. Also, some processes can be automated through other means. Consider the very simple example of sending automated emails, or sorting out your inbox by putting the right email in the right folder, those types of things can be done with email rules rather than RPA.
If a platform already has some sort of inbuilt automation, whether that's a social media platform, email platform, networking platform, or any other type of platform, it's always better to explore that first before looking to solve that problem with RPA. There are times when an Excel Macro or an email rule will be a lot faster and a lot more cost-efficient. RPA should be directed towards big-ticket items, big problems, and large volumes to where no existing solution would provide the same level of value.
My advice for anybody who is considering UiPath is to try it out for themselves. The most beautiful thing is when companies take the leap to have a very small citizen developer team, where they upskill a few technically-minded people with free courses and try to build a small proof of concept to see if RPA is the right path for them. I really encourage that sort of curiosity and experimentation because all of the resources are out there and anybody can learn, as long as they're driven and passionate and curious about automation. I would really encourage people just to give it a try and see what comes out of it.
In our organization, UiPath is the number one RPA tool. Being close to the industry as a developer, and I do feel like it's the preferred tool, at least where I'm based in Australia. It is definitely the preferred RPA solution on the market. Our usage is definitely going to increase in the future. I feel like the future is bright for UiPath. That said, it isn't perfect.
I would rate this solution a nine out of ten.
